name: How does Colorado's dry climate affect interior marble tile installations?

mainEntity.name: How does Colorado's dry climate affect interior marble tile installations?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Colorado, seasonal indoor humidity drops dramatically in winter due to cold outdoor air and indoor heating, which causes subfloors to expand and contract. Natural marble has no give, so dry subfloor shifting can crack tiles if an uncoupling membrane is omitted. Additionally, rapid winter evaporation can draw moisture out of thin-set mortar too quickly if jobsite temperatures and drying conditions are not monitored. Proper indoor climate control and specialized crack-isolation layers protect the installation from seasonal shifting in Denver-area homes.
acceptedAnswer.description: Dry indoor air and seasonal humidity shifts cause subfloor movement. Using uncoupling membranes and controlling room temperatures prevents mortar drying issues and cracked tiles.
